items.question: Can I change plans later?
items.answer: Yes. Upgrades apply immediately and are prorated; downgrades take effect at the end of the billing period.

items.question: What counts as a pageview?
items.answer: Every page load that reaches your site, including each page change in a single-page app. Bots and your own visits are filtered out.

items.question: Is there a discount for non-profits?
items.answer: Registered non-profits and open-source projects get the Team plan at half price. Write to us with a link to your organisation.

items.question: Which payment methods do you accept?
items.answer: Credit card and SEPA direct debit for all plans, invoice with bank transfer for Enterprise.

items.question: What happens when I exceed my pageviews?
items.answer: We keep collecting and send you a note. You can upgrade within 30 days; nothing is switched off in the meantime.

title: Harbor Line
meta_description: How Harbor Line replaced a heavy ticket shop with a fast timetable: 82 percent lighter, 31 percent more bookings.

data.text: Harbor Line: a booking site that loads before the ferry leaves

data.html: How a regional ferry operator replaced a heavy ticket shop with a timetable that works on a harbour-side connection.

data.alt: Illustration of a striped lighthouse and sailboats on a teal sea beneath a low sun

data.html: Most visitors arrive on a phone, standing on a quay, with one bar of signal. The old site asked for 4.8 MB before it showed a single departure, and the booking flow lost people at the second step.

We started with the timetable, because that is what people open the site for, and made it the first screen.

  • A server-rendered timetable that needs no script to read.
  • One booking step per screen, with errors explained in plain words.
  • Images sized for the device and loaded only when they scroll into view.

data.text: We stopped getting calls that began with “the site is stuck”. That alone paid for the project.
data.author: Mara Lindqvist

data.html: Start from the one task that matters, measure on the slowest realistic device and write error messages before writing code. None of it is clever, and all of it compounds.

title: Tidewater Bank
meta_description: How Tidewater Bank rebuilt its loan application around plain language and keyboard access.

data.text: Tidewater Bank: calmer forms, fewer support calls

data.html: A credit union rebuilt its loan application around plain language, clear errors and full keyboard access.

data.alt: Abstract illustration in calm blue shapes suggesting a bank counter

data.html: Session recordings showed the same pattern: people reached the income question, hesitated and called us. The label said “Net equivalised household income”.
Every question now says what we need and why, errors sit next to the field and explain how to fix it, and the whole flow works without a mouse.

data.html: Everything you need to collect, read and share your numbers. Start with the quick start; the guides go deeper.

  • Configuration: every option in one table
  • Guides: custom events and data export
  • Changelog: what changed and when

title: Getting started
meta_description: Create a site, add one line of code and see your first pageview in five minutes.

data.html: Add one line to your site and see your first pageview in under five minutes.
Sign in, choose Add site and enter your domain. Tidepool shows a snippet that is unique to the site.
Paste the snippet into the <head> of every page. It loads asynchronously and weighs less than 2 KB.
Open your site in a new tab. Within a few seconds the Live view shows one visitor: you.
Disable content blockers for your own site, confirm the site id and check the browser console for a blocked request.

title: Installation
meta_description: Add Tidepool with a script tag, the npm package or server-side events.

data.html: Three ways to add Tidepool. Pick the one that matches how your site is built.
Best for static sites and most content management systems. See Getting started for the snippet.
For applications with a build step. Install the package and call init once.
Send events from your backend with one HTTP request. No cookies are involved.
Events appear in Live within seconds. A 401 response means the key is wrong or expired.

title: Configuration
meta_description: Every Tidepool option with its default value, privacy defaults and page exclusion patterns.

data.html: Every option Tidepool understands, with its default.

OptionDefaultWhat it does
sitenoneYour site id. Required.
hashfalseCount hash changes as pageviews.
respectDnttrueSkip visitors who send Do Not Track.
exclude[]Path patterns that are never counted.
Tidepool sets no cookies and stores no personal data. IP addresses are used to derive a country and then discarded.
Patterns use * as a wildcard. Internal tools and previews are good candidates.

title: Guides
meta_description: Task-focused guides for Tidepool: custom events and data export.

data.html: Task-focused walkthroughs for when the basics are in place.

• Custom events: track what matters to your product
  • Data export: take your numbers elsewhere

title: Custom events
meta_description: Track custom events with Tidepool: sending, naming and reading them in reports.

data.html: Pageviews tell you what was read. Events tell you what was done.
Call track with a name and optional properties.
Use short, past-tense names such as signup or invoice_paid. A small, stable vocabulary keeps reports readable.
Properties are flat key-value pairs. Avoid personal data; Tidepool does not need it.
Open Events in the sidebar, pick a name and split it by any property.

title: Data export
meta_description: Export Tidepool data as CSV or JSON from the dashboard or through the API.

data.html: Your numbers are yours. Export them any time, in a format other tools understand.
Open any report, choose Export and pick CSV or JSON. The export covers the date range on screen.
For recurring exports, request the raw events with a read-only key.
Exports are limited to ten requests per minute per key. Larger ranges are paged.

title: Changelog
meta_description: Release notes for Tidepool, newest first.

data.html: What changed in Tidepool, newest first.

Added12 October 2026

Shared dashboards can now be embedded in other sites. Weekly digests now come as plain text too.

Fixed21 September 2026

Fixed a rounding error in the visitor count for sites with more than one million pageviews.

Added2 September 2026

Custom events accept up to ten properties. The Events report can be split by any property.

Changed14 July 2026

The tracking script is now 1.6 KB, down from 2.3 KB, and no longer blocks rendering.
